 Learn more Strategy's mNAV Is "Now Below 1," Says Peter Schiff. That Breaks Saylor's Favorite Trade ©@Karola G from Pexels via Canva, @Karola G from Pexels via Canva Key Takeaways 
 Peter Schiff says Strategy's mNAV is now below 1, with its STRC preferred trading below $96. 
 Strategy's 12 straight weeks of gains in bitcoin per share came from selling stock above its bitcoin value, which stops working below 1. 
 Michael Saylor says Strategy will keep buying back STRC below $100, so the money now comes from its USD assets or its bitcoin. 
 A Strategy forced to sell would hurt MARA Holdings, already selling bitcoin, and Coinbase, which needs crypto trading to recover. 
 Strategy ( MSTR:NASDAQ ) can only grow its bitcoin per share by selling stock if that stock trades above the value of its bitcoin. Peter Schiff says it doesn't anymore. 
 "The highly touted mNAV of Strategy is now below 1," the longtime bitcoin critic posted on X on Thursday. "Given yesterday's heavy sell volume in $STRC, and its current share price below $96, it looks like the entire $MSTR ecosystem is about to blow up." (STRC is Strategy's 12% perpetual preferred.) 
 He called Strategy possibly "the pin that pricks not just the Bitcoin bubble, but all of crypto." That would reach Coinbase ( COIN:NASDAQ ) , whose revenue still rides on crypto trading, and MARA Holdings ( MARA:NASDAQ ) , which is already selling bitcoin to pay down its debt. 
 I think "blow up" goes too far. But Schiff is right that Strategy can't run Saylor's favorite trade at this price. 
 Twelve good weeks, paid for with stock 
 Earlier the same day, Strategy posted its own scorecard : "Our swaps increased Net BTC per Share in each of the last 12 weeks." Selling MSTR above its net bitcoin value and buying back STRC below $100 added about 580 sats (hundred-millionths of a bitcoin) per common share before preferred dividends, it said. 
 That took a lot of stock. Strategy's diluted share count nearly doubled from the end of 2024 to the third quarter of 2026: 
 Strategy (MSTR): diluted shares outstanding, millions of shares, last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR) The selling kept going into November. In the week to Nov. 15, Strategy sold $244.7 million of common stock , and Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said it bought back $228 million of STRC.

 The premium is gone 
 Below 1, each new share brings in less cash than the bitcoin it claims, so every sale leaves less bitcoin for the shares already out there. Management set an even higher bar: on its first-quarter call in May, it put the break-even for buying bitcoin with new stock at 1.22x mNAV. 
 Story Continues Bitcoin made up 94.5% of Strategy's assets at June 30, so its book value moves with bitcoin. The stock now trades at 0.7x book, its lowest in three years, against a three-year average of 6.1x: 
 Strategy (MSTR): price/book value, last 3 years (TIKR) That's a long way from 25.4x in November 2024. 
 Now Strategy pays with cash or bitcoin 
 Saylor isn't backing off. "We intend to keep buying below $100," he posted on Thursday, adding that buybacks "lower dividend obligations." Schiff expects Strategy to "blow through its cash reserve to buy more, then start selling Bitcoin to buy what's left." 
 Strategy had built cash and short-term investments of $5.91 billion by Sept. 30: 
 Strategy (MSTR): cash and short-term investments, $ billions, last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR) Saylor put its USD assets at $4.9 billion as of Nov. 15 and says that at today's rates they "can fund 3.4 years of interest and dividends." Every STRC buyback below $100 now comes out of that cushion, unless Strategy keeps selling stock and accepts less bitcoin per share. Once the cash runs low, bitcoin is next. 
 Strategy wouldn't be selling alone 
 MARA is already doing what Schiff expects Strategy to do. After the third quarter, it sold bitcoin to repay $750 million of bitcoin-backed debt, according to its third-quarter shareholder letter, and it plans to keep using bitcoin to build cash for next year's convertible-note puts and a new $500 million buyback. 
 Coinbase's third-quarter transaction revenue was already down 44% from a year earlier. Analysts expect a normalized loss of $0.32 a share for 2026, then $2.46 of earnings in 2027, and that rebound needs crypto trading to pick up. A Strategy forced to sell some of its 850,849 bitcoin would be bad news for both. 
 Saylor needs the premium back 
 "Blow up" is too strong for a company with billions in cash and no obligation to buy back a single share of STRC. But until the stock trades above its bitcoin again, I'd treat Strategy as a leveraged bitcoin holder spending down its cash, and I'd watch next Monday's update to see how far that cushion drops. 
 Of course, bitcoin can close the gap quickly, and an mNAV back above 1 puts the swap right back on the table.
